paper_metadata.title: Lower Oxygen Tension and Intracranial Hemorrhage in Venovenous Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the setting, recruitment period, and inclusion/exclusion criteria. However, as a retrospective analysis from a single tertiary center, there is a risk of selection bias. The participation rate of eligible individuals is not explicitly stated, making it difficult to determine if the sample is truly representative of the broader VV-ECMO population.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factors (PaO2 and PaCO2) are measured using objective arterial blood gas (ABG) tests. The study uses a high frequency of measurement (every 2-4 hours) and defines the PF using medians over a 24-hour window, which reduces the impact of single-point fluctuations.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Pre- and post-cannulation ABG values were defined as the median of all PaCO2 and PaO2 values, respectively, 24 hours before and after cannulation.
items.reasoning: The PF is clearly defined both as a continuous median and a categorical threshold (<70 mmHg).

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: ABGs were obtained every 2–4 hours.
items.reasoning: ABG is the gold standard for measuring oxygen and carbon dioxide tension.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: Hypoxemia post-cannulation was defined as a median post-cannulation PaO2 value <70 mmHg14.
items.reasoning: The authors used a pre-defined threshold based on literature (reference 14) rather than a data-driven cut-point.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses multivariable logistic regression to control for PaCO2 when assessing PaO2. However, other critical confounders such as anticoagulation levels (heparin), platelet counts, and blood pressure—all of which are known to influence ICH risk—were not included in the multivariable model, likely due to the small number of events (n=14 ICH).

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical analysis is generally appropriate, but the small number of ICH events (n=14) limits the number of variables that can be included in the multivariable model without overfitting. The authors acknowledge this limitation. There is no evidence of selective reporting, as both PaO2 and PaCO2 results are presented.
